newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire opposition envisages dialogue with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Zaire opposition envisages dialogue with rebels.

text.p: Zaire's radical opposition is considering sending an envoy to hold peace talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila, whose forces control towns and territory in the east.
But the government, which has thrown its weight behind a military solution, says peace talks are out of the question while Zairean territory remains in rebel hands.

"The radical opposition envisages sending an envoy to Laurent Kabila who is just one frustrated Zairean among many others," the head of the radical opposition's parliamentary group told Reuters, saying dialogue was the one viable option.
"We must above all save lives," Joseph Olenghankoy said in a telephone interview late on Saturday. "Only negotiations will give us a way out of this war."

Veteran radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi, head of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS), floated the idea of dialogue with Kabila after reconciliation talks with President Mobutu Sese Seko in France at the end of last year.
For Tshisekedi, whose reconciliation with Mobutu was short-lived, the solution to the crisis is a government of national unity grouping all the main political tendencies.
Tshisekedi supporters had hoped Mobutu would name him at the head of a new government when he returned in December from four months in Europe and cancer surgery.

Mobutu, who has since returned to Europe for more medical tests, stuck with Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, Tshisekedi's arch rival, who has won favour in the West for his efforts to control Zaire's corruption-plagued economy.

The rebels, who launched their revolt in October, drove Zaire's poorly paid and ill-disciplined army back in disarray. They control eastern towns of Goma, Uvira, Bukavu and Bunia and territory along the border with Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda.
Kabila has invited the central government in Kinshasa to go to Goma, his headquarters, for negotiations, within the framework of a national conference.
The government and the army favour the military option.
"There will be no negotiation with Laurent Kabila so long as the aggressors occupy a large part of eastern Zaire," Foreign Minister Gerard Kamanda wa Kamanda told Reuters on Saturday
The army and the defence ministry say they are preparing for a major counter-offensive to retake occupied territory.
They have remained silent about the timing but Zairean newspapers had predicted a thrust this weekend.

The new chief of staff, General Mahele Bokoungo Lieko, appointed by Mobutu on December 18 with wider powers than his predecessors, is currently in Kisangani, capital of Haut-Zaire province, organising his troops.
The army has made Kisangani, which controls the road to the front line, a control and supply base for its promised counter-attack.
